The system comprises a frame extending in longitudinal, transverse, and vertical directions. The frame includes two longitudinal girders connected by multiple pairs of transverse primary support beams. The invention relates to a frame-based transport system designed for carrying large, heavy, or irregularly shaped items, particularly annular components such as industrial flanges. The system comprises at least two longitudinal girders extending in the direction of transport and a plurality of transverse support beams arranged in pairs between or across the longitudinal girders. Each pair of transverse support beams defines a storage area for receiving and supporting one or more items.

The transverse support beams are positioned so that the storage areas remain accessible from below. This downward access allows lifting equipment, such as the forks of a forklift truck or another suitable handling device, to engage an item from underneath. As a result, heavy components can be inserted into or removed from the frame without requiring extensive dismantling of the transport system. The spacing and configuration of the support beams may be selected according to the dimensions, weight, and shape of the items being transported.

The longitudinal girders and transverse support beams together form a rigid load-bearing structure capable of distributing the weight of the stored items across the frame. Where annular items such as flanges are transported, the support beams may engage opposite portions of each item and hold it in a stable position. Additional retaining elements, stops, fastening devices, or securing straps may be used to prevent lateral, longitudinal, or vertical movement during handling and transport.

The external dimensions of the frame are selected to correspond to standard freight-container dimensions or standardized container-interface locations. The frame can therefore be placed on top of a freight container without requiring a specially designed transport platform. Compatible locking mechanisms, such as container corner fittings and twist-lock devices, may be provided at appropriate positions on the frame. These mechanisms permit the frame to be releasably but securely connected to the upper corner fittings of the container.

Once mounted and locked in place, the frame and the underlying container form a stable transport unit suitable for movement by road, rail, or sea. The standardized interface also allows conventional container-handling equipment to be used during loading, unloading, stacking, and transfer operations. Depending on the configuration, the frame may be removed from the container as a complete unit, allowing the transported items to remain secured within the frame until they are required at their destination.

By combining a rigid support frame, downwardly accessible storage areas, and standardized container-compatible fastening points, the invention simplifies the handling of large industrial components. It reduces the need for custom packaging, improves load security, and makes efficient use of existing freight-container infrastructure. The system consequently provides a safe, flexible, and economical solution for transporting flanges and other bulky or heavy items.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest yet most important words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a particular person, place, object, or idea. There is a meaningful difference between saying “a book” and “the book”: the first can refer to any book, while the second points to a specific one.

Despite its simplicity, “the” gives language precision and context. It helps speakers connect through shared knowledge, directing attention toward something already known or understood. This modest three-letter word demonstrates how even the simplest parts of language can shape meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a formal technical description of a transport frame (100) that has longitudinal girders (6, 6′), paired transversal primary support beams, downward access to stored items, and a lower section dimensioned to lock securely onto a standard freight container.
counterfactuals.output:
A transport frame (100) comprises a load-bearing structure having two substantially parallel longitudinal girders (6, 6′) extending in a longitudinal direction of the frame. A plurality of transversal primary support beams is arranged in pairs at spaced positions along the longitudinal girders (6, 6′). Each pair of primary support beams extends transversely between, and is structurally connected to, the longitudinal girders so as to define a respective storage position for receiving and supporting one or more transportable items.

The primary support beams are configured to support the stored items without obstructing a downward removal path. Accordingly, each storage position includes a downwardly open access region through which a stored item may be lowered or withdrawn from the transport frame (100), for example by suitable lifting or handling equipment positioned beneath the frame. Retaining, guiding, or releasable locking elements may be provided at the storage positions to secure the items during transport while permitting their controlled release for downward unloading.

A lower section of the transport frame (100) has an external footprint and interface geometry corresponding to those of a standard freight container. The lower section includes locking interfaces positioned to cooperate with standardized container securing points, such as corner castings and associated twist-lock devices. The transport frame (100) can thereby be seated on and positively locked to the upper securing points of a standard freight container, with longitudinal, transverse, and vertical displacement being restrained during handling and transportation. The longitudinal girders (6, 6′), paired transversal primary support beams, and lower section together form a rigid structure capable of transferring the weight of the stored items and transport-induced loads into the freight container through the standardized locking interfaces.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for safely transporting large industrial components on top of a shipping container. Include coordinate directions X, Y, and Z, numbered structural elements, upper and lower surfaces, and twist-lock-style container securing features.
counterfactuals.output:
### Container-Mounted Transport Cradle

An invention comprises a removable transport cradle **(100)** for safely carrying a large industrial component **(10)** on top of an ISO shipping container **(20)**. The cradle distributes weight into the container’s corner castings while restraining the component against longitudinal, lateral, and vertical movement.

#### Coordinate system

- **X direction:** longitudinal direction, parallel to the container length.  
- **Y direction:** transverse direction, parallel to the container width.  
- **Z direction:** vertical direction, perpendicular to the container roof.

#### Structural elements

The cradle **(100)** includes:

1. Two longitudinal beams **(110)** extending in the X direction.
2. Multiple transverse beams **(120)** extending in the Y direction between the longitudinal beams **(110)**.
3. Four corner support assemblies **(130)** positioned over the upper corner castings **(22)** of the container **(20)**.
4. Component-support saddles **(140)** mounted above the beams and shaped to receive the industrial component **(10)**.
5. Adjustable restraints **(150)** that limit movement of the component in the X, Y, and Z directions.
6. Diagonal braces **(160)** for transferring acceleration and braking loads between the saddles **(140)** and corner support assemblies **(130)**.
7. Optional access platforms and lifting eyes **(170)**.

Each longitudinal beam **(110)** and transverse beam **(120)** has an **upper surface (112, 122)** facing generally in the positive Z direction and a **lower surface (114, 124)** facing the container roof. Replaceable pads **(132)** on the lower surfaces of the corner support assemblies maintain clearance between the structural beams and the relatively weak roof sheet.

#### Container attachment

Each corner support assembly **(130)** includes a downwardly projecting, twist-lock-style securing feature **(134)**. The securing feature enters an aperture in a corresponding upper corner casting **(22)** and includes a rotatable locking head **(136)**. After insertion, the locking head is rotated—typically about the Z axis—to an engaged position beneath an internal retaining surface of the corner casting. A handle, hydraulic actuator, or other operator **(138)** moves the head between locked and unlocked positions.

A lock indicator **(139)** visibly identifies whether each securing feature is fully engaged. Secondary locking pins prevent accidental rotation. Thus, vertical uplift loads are resisted through the twist-lock-style securing features, while X- and Y-direction loads are transferred through contact between the corner support assemblies and the corner castings.

#### Component retention

The saddles **(140)** may slide in the X direction along indexed mounting locations and may be adjusted in the Y and Z directions to accommodate components of different sizes. Each saddle has an upper support surface **(142)** with an elastomeric liner and a lower mounting surface **(144)** secured to the beams.

Clamps or tension members **(150)** extend over or around the component **(10)** and connect to reinforced anchor points **(152)**. End stops **(154)** resist X-direction movement, side guides **(156)** resist Y-direction movement, and hold-down members **(158)** resist positive Z-direction movement and overturning.

Loads are therefore directed into the container’s structural corner castings rather than into the upper roof surface, permitting the component and cradle to be handled as a secured containerized transport unit.

## Title

**Transportation Rack for Flanged Components**

## Abstract

A transportation rack (10) for storing and transporting flanged components comprises a longitudinal frame (12) extending in a longitudinal direction and a plurality of transverse support-beam pairs (20) spaced along the longitudinal frame. Each support-beam pair comprises first and second transverse support beams (22, 24) arranged to support respective portions of at least one flanged component and to define a corresponding storage area (26). The frame and the support beams are arranged such that a downwardly open access region (28) is provided beneath each storage area, thereby permitting lifting equipment to access a supported flanged component from below without obstruction by a floor or other permanent cross-member. A base (30) of the rack has external dimensions corresponding to freight-container dimensions and comprises locking interfaces (32), such as standardized corner fittings, positioned for engagement with freight-container locking devices. The rack can therefore be handled, stacked and secured using existing intermodal freight-container infrastructure.

## Claims

1. **A transportation rack (10) for receiving flanged components, the transportation rack comprising:**
   
   a longitudinal frame (12) extending in a longitudinal direction;
   
   a plurality of transverse support-beam pairs (20) arranged at positions spaced apart in the longitudinal direction, each transverse support-beam pair (20) comprising a first transverse support beam (22) and a second transverse support beam (24) and defining a storage area (26) for at least one flanged component;
   
   wherein the first and second transverse support beams (22, 24) are configured to support spaced portions of the at least one flanged component;
   
   wherein the longitudinal frame (12) and the transverse support-beam pairs (20) define, beneath the respective storage areas (26), downwardly open access regions (28) that are free from permanent structural members obstructing access to the supported flanged component from below; and
   
   a base (30) having external dimensions selected in accordance with standardized freight-container dimensions and comprising locking interfaces (32) positioned and configured for engagement with standardized freight-container locking devices.

2. The transportation rack according to claim 1, wherein the locking interfaces (32) comprise corner fittings configured to receive twist-lock elements.

3. The transportation rack according to claim 1 or claim 2, wherein the external dimensions and the positions of the locking interfaces (32) conform to an intermodal freight-container standard.

4. The transportation rack according to any preceding claim, wherein each storage area (26) is open at least downwardly and laterally to permit insertion of lifting members beneath a flanged component supported in the storage area.

5. The transportation rack according to any preceding claim, wherein the first and second transverse support beams (22, 24) of each support-beam pair are spaced apart in the longitudinal direction.

6. The transportation rack according to any preceding claim, wherein at least one of the transverse support beams (22, 24) is removably or adjustably connected to the longitudinal frame (12), such that a spacing or position of the transverse support beams is adjustable to accommodate flanged components of different dimensions.

7. The transportation rack according to any preceding claim, wherein each transverse support beam (22, 24) comprises at least one support formation (34) configured to engage a circumferential flange, a hub, a neck or a body portion of the flanged component.

8. The transportation rack according to claim 7, wherein the support formation (34) comprises a cradle, recess, saddle or inclined support surface.

9. The transportation rack according to claim 7 or claim 8, wherein the support formation (34) comprises a resilient or non-metallic contact layer.

10. The transportation rack according to any preceding claim, comprising at least one retaining device (36) configured to inhibit movement of a flanged component relative to the transverse support-beam pair during transportation.

11. The transportation rack according to claim 10, wherein the retaining device (36) comprises at least one of a strap, chain, clamp, chock, pin or removable retaining bar.

12. The transportation rack according to any preceding claim, wherein the longitudinal frame (12) comprises first and second longitudinal base members (14, 16) extending along opposite lateral sides of the rack, the downwardly open access regions (28) being located between the first and second longitudinal base members.

13. The transportation rack according to any preceding claim, comprising upright members (40) extending from the base (30) and upper stacking interfaces (42) arranged for engagement with another transportation rack or with freight-container handling equipment.

14. The transportation rack according to claim 13, wherein the upright members (40), the base (30) and the upper stacking interfaces (42) define an outer envelope corresponding to an outer envelope of a standardized freight container.

15. The transportation rack according to any preceding claim, wherein the rack is free from a continuous floor beneath the storage areas (26).

16. The transportation rack according to any preceding claim, wherein each downwardly open access region (28) is dimensioned to receive one or more lifting arms, forklift tines, lifting slings or other lifting members from below.

17. The transportation rack according to any preceding claim, wherein the rack is configured to support a plurality of pipe spools, valves, flanged fittings or other elongate components having one or more flanges.

18. **A transportation assembly comprising:**
   
   a transportation rack (10) according to any preceding claim; and
   
   at least one flanged component supported by one of the transverse support-beam pairs (20),
   
   wherein a lower portion of the flanged component is accessible through the downwardly open access region (28).

19. **A method of handling a flanged component, the method comprising:**
   
   supporting the flanged component on a transverse support-beam pair (20) of a transportation rack (10), the transportation rack having a base (30) configured according to standardized freight-container dimensions and locking standards;
   
   transporting or securing the transportation rack using freight-container handling or locking equipment;
   
   introducing at least one lifting member into a downwardly open access region (28) beneath the flanged component; and
   
   lifting the flanged component from the transverse support-beam pair using the at least one lifting member.

20. The method according to claim 19, wherein introducing the at least one lifting member is performed without removing a floor panel or a permanent transverse structural member from the transportation rack.

## Description

### Technical field

The invention relates to racks for storing, handling and transporting industrial components, particularly components comprising one or more flanges, such as pipe spools, valves, fittings, pressure-vessel components and tubular assemblies. The invention more particularly relates to a transportation rack compatible with intermodal freight-container handling and securing systems.

### Background

Flanged components are often transported on pallets, in crates or in enclosed freight containers. Such arrangements may provide inadequate support for components of different shapes and may restrict access to the underside of a component. Removal can therefore require manual repositioning, disassembly of the supporting structure or the use of lifting equipment from above.

There is a need for a transportation rack that supports flanged components in defined storage areas while allowing lifting equipment to access the components from below. It is also desirable for the rack to be transportable and securable using existing freight-container infrastructure.

### Summary of the invention

The transportation rack comprises a longitudinal frame and a plurality of transverse support-beam pairs spaced along the frame. Each pair defines a storage area and supports spaced portions of a flanged component. The region beneath each storage area remains substantially unobstructed and is open downwardly, so that lifting members can be positioned beneath the component.

The rack further comprises a base dimensioned in accordance with a standardized freight-container footprint. Locking interfaces, for example corner fittings compatible with twist-lock devices, are provided at standardized positions. The rack may consequently be secured to a vehicle, vessel, rail wagon, handling platform or another rack using conventional freight-container locking equipment.

In this context, “unobstructed” does not necessarily require the complete absence of every rack element beneath a storage area. Rather, it denotes that no permanent structural member extends across the intended access path in a manner that prevents the designated lifting equipment from reaching and lifting the supported component from below.

The standardized freight-container dimensions and locking interfaces may conform to applicable ISO intermodal-container standards, including standards relating to container dimensions, ratings and corner fittings. The rack may have the footprint of, for example, a 10-foot, 20-foot or 40-foot freight container, while being open-sided and optionally open-topped.
